万.meaning: A <part>one</part>-plank shelf runs across the top of a bank vault, and from it a hooked chute bends down into a long <part>slash</part> of a slide. Coins pour down it all night, clinking into a pile, until the counter finally clicks over: <kanji>ten thousand</kanji>.
万.on: A cheeky <sound>mon</sound>key slides down after the coins and stuffs its cheeks with them, counting every one.
万.kun: The monkey trades the lot for a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt, a pet <sound>ro</sound>dent and a ticket to the <sound>zoo</sound>.

格.meaning: Beside a <part>tree</part>, <part>each</part> guest arrives in turn, and the tree sorts them onto its branches: kings at the very top, knights in the middle, the rest of us down on the roots. Where you sit shows your <kanji>status</kanji>.
格.on: Vultures in the tree know their status too: the top bird gets the best bit of the <sound>carc</sound>ass, the lowest gets the bones.

氏.meaning: A banner hangs from a hooked pole, drooping to one side, with a small knot dangling under its bar. It is stitched with a single word, the name every cousin, aunt and grandson shares: the <kanji>family name</kanji>.
氏.on: The family name is painted in gold right across a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
氏.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasp the cousins, as the banner rolls past on the back of a <sound>jee</sound>p.

民.meaning: Under the <part>clan</part> banner, a crowd gathers and opens one big <part>mouth</part>: farmers, bakers, children, all shouting together. No kings or lords here, just ordinary <kanji>people</kanji>.
民.on: The people chase a <sound>mean</sound> giant out of town for stealing all the bread.
民.kun: Then they share one enormous <sound>ta</sound>co with a hungry <sound>mee</sound>rkat.

紙.meaning: A <part>clan</part> of beavers chews <part>thread</part> and bark into mush, spreads it flat on a rock and leaves it in the sun. Next morning they peel off a thin white sheet you can write on: <kanji>paper</kanji>.
紙.on: A knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld turns out to be made of paper, and the first raindrop goes straight through it.
紙.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp folds the paper into a hat and plops it on a <sound>mee</sound>rkat's head.

温.meaning: You pour <part>water drops</part> into a <part>dish</part> and set it out under the <part>sun</part>. By lunchtime the water is just right for your toes: not cold, not hot, but nice and <kanji>warm</kanji>.
温.on: Too slow? Flip the heater's <sound>on</sound> switch, and the dish starts to steam.
温.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' you sigh, toes in the warm dish, while a drummer beside you taps softly: '<sound>ta</sound>, <sound>ta</sound>.'

配.meaning: A <part>cobra</part> slithers from house to house with a crate of <part>dynamite</part>, leaving one stick on every doorstep. Nobody asked for one, but everybody gets one. That's how you <kanji>distribute</kanji> things.
配.on: Next it hands out jars of honey, one from every <sound>hi</sound>ve in the village.
配.kun: '<sound>Cu</sound>ckoo!' calls a clock, and a sheep bleats '<sound>Bah</sound>!' as each one gets its share.

重.meaning: A farmer tries to lift his whole <part>farm</part> onto his back, with a <part>thousand</part> sacks of potatoes piled on top. His knees wobble and his face goes red. It's far too <kanji>heavy</kanji>.
重.on: Right on top of the pile sits a single tiny <sound>jew</sound>el, and somehow that's the heaviest thing of all.
重.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' groans the farmer, as a <sound>mo</sound>le pops up and adds one more potato.

誰.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> lands on the podium in the middle of your <part>speech</part> and starts to chirp. Everyone stares at it, then at you. Is this your bird? The sparrow tilts its head and asks right back: <kanji>who</kanji> are you?
誰.on: Who left a <sound>swee</sound>t on the podium? The sparrow pecks the wrapper open.
誰.kun: Who threw these <sound>da</sound>rts? One just popped a <sound>re</sound>d balloon over the sparrow's head.

台.meaning: A statue poses with its <part>elbow</part> bent on top of a box shaped like a big <part>mouth</part>. The mouth grumbles, 'You're heavy!', but the statue won't budge. It's far too proud of its <kanji>pedestal</kanji>.
台.on: A pair of <sound>di</sound>ce rolls off the pedestal and lands on double six.
台.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasps the crowd, as the statue swings a <sound>te</sound>nnis racket at a flying <sound>na</sound>an.

進.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> hops up a <part>ramp</part>, one step at a time, never back. A gust blows; it leans into the wind and keeps on going. Every hop takes it a little higher. It can only <kanji>advance</kanji>.
進.on: Halfway up, it bumps its little <sound>shin</sound> on a pebble, but it doesn't stop.
進.kun: At the top it finds a <sound>su</sound>shi bar and a bowl of <sound>su</sound>gar, its prize for getting this far.

早.meaning: The <part>sun</part> climbs onto a big wooden cross, a <part>ten</part>, to peek over the hill before anyone else is up. The birds aren't even singing yet and the milk hasn't come. It's very <kanji>early</kanji>.
早.on: Half asleep, you reach for the <sound>soa</sound>p and knock it down the drain.
早.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the rooster, already wide awake and knitting a scarf of <sound>ya</sound>rn.

伝.meaning: A messenger hangs his coat on a <part>coat hook</part>, ties a note to a <part>kite</part> and lets it fly over the hills to the next village. There, someone reads it, ties on a new note and sends it on. That's how you <kanji>transmit</kanji> news.
伝.on: The kite lands on a <sound>den</sound>tist's chair, and the dentist reads the note aloud to his patient.
伝.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the patient, and blows the note onto a <sound>ta</sound>co.

四.meaning: Inside a <part>cage</part>, a pair of <part>legs</part> paces round and round, bumping into every wall in turn: front, back, left, right. One, two, three, <kanji>four</kanji>. No way out.
四.on: The prisoner props a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld against each of the four walls.
四.kun: To pass the time, the legs practise karate kicks at the walls: '<sound>Yot</sound>! <sound>Tsu</sound>!'

皮.meaning: On a hot day, a bear hooks the top of its fur coat on a post and wriggles out, twisting like a <part>pretzel</part>. It leaves the empty coat dangling and goes for a swim. Left behind: one furry <kanji>pelt</kanji>.
皮.on: A fox tries on the pelt and struts about on one tall <sound>hee</sound>l.
皮.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp spots the bare bear in the river and cries '<sound>Wah</sound>! Where's your fur?'

彼.meaning: Someone rides up the <part>chairlift</part> wrapped in a huge furry <part>pelt</part>. You squint up from the bottom. Is that a bear? No, it's that fellow from next door. Look, there <kanji>he</kanji> goes.
彼.on: At the top he hops off, wobbling on one tall <sound>hee</sound>l.
彼.kun: He waves at you from a little <sound>ca</sound>rt painted bright <sound>re</sound>d.

教.meaning: Out of <part>filial piety</part>, a boy lets his old grandpa lean on his shoulder. In return, grandpa points his folding <part>fan</part> at the blackboard: letters, sums, the names of the stars. The old man loves to <kanji>teach</kanji>.
教.on: Class starts when grandpa's pet owl gives one long, sleepy '<sound>Kyooh</sound>!'
教.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' says the boy, finally getting it, and draws a <sound>shee</sound>p on the board.

転.meaning: A <part>kite</part> string gets tangled round the wheel of a <part>car</part>. The car spins round and round, the kite loops in circles above it, and the driver gets dizzy. Everything starts to <kanji>revolve</kanji>.
転.on: A <sound>ten</sound>or on the roof spins with it, singing one long note the whole time.
転.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala and a <sound>ro</sound>dent cling to the bumper as the car rolls off downhill.

送.meaning: An <part>alien</part> stands at the foot of a <part>ramp</part> with a parcel under each arm, pushes them up into its little spaceship and waves them off to its mum on Mars. Every week it has something to <kanji>send</kanji>.
送.on: This week's parcel is a giant bar of <sound>soa</sound>p, because Mars is very dusty.
送.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' says its mum, opening the box, and out pops a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo.

住.meaning: A <part>lord</part> hangs his cloak on the <part>coat hook</part> by the door, kicks off his boots and puts his feet up. This isn't a visit: his name is on the mailbox. This is the house where he will <kanji>dwell</kanji>.
住.on: He keeps his best <sound>jew</sound>el on the mantelpiece, so everyone knows this is his home.
住.kun: Every night he eats <sound>su</sound>shi in his slippers by the fire.

亡.meaning: An old sailor lies down in a long wooden <part>drawer</part> for his final rest, and his friends set a <part>lid</part> with a little knob on top. They hum his favourite song and say goodbye to the <kanji>deceased</kanji>.
亡.on: They roll a <sound>bou</sound>lder up beside the grave to mark the spot.
亡.kun: On the boulder they leave his last <sound>na</sound>an, for the journey.

忘.meaning: A <part>tombstone</part> sits right on top of your <part>heart</part>, pressing down on everything you once knew: your keys, your homework, your best friend's birthday. All of it buried. You <kanji>forget</kanji>.
忘.on: A <sound>bou</sound>lder sits in your path, and you walk straight into it: you forgot it was there.
忘.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' you cry, halfway through lunch: you forgot the soy sauce for your <sound>su</sound>shi.

杯.meaning: At a picnic under a <part>tree</part>, you lift a jam jar to make a toast, and the tree waves a <part>negative</part> sign: no, not like that! It drops a glass from a branch, tall-stemmed and shining: a proper <kanji>wine glass</kanji>.
杯.on: The bees from a nearby <sound>hi</sound>ve buzz down to clink glasses with you.
杯.kun: You raise your glass with a <sound>sa</sound>rdine, a <sound>ca</sound>rp, a seal from the <sound>zoo</sound> and a man holding a golden <sound>key</sound>.

差.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> stands on a <part>workbench</part> to be measured against its twin, and a <part>slash</part> of chalk marks where each head comes up to. One is a hair taller. The judge squints at the tiny <kanji>distinction</kanji>.
差.on: The twins get a prize anyway: one <sound>sa</sound>rdine each, exactly the same size.
差.kun: The judge raises a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and points it at the taller twin: to point, to hold up.

故.meaning: An <part>old</part> man waves a <part>fan</part> to cool himself, and the breeze knocks a teacup off the shelf, which rolls into a cat, which leaps into the soup. Nobody meant any of it. It was all <kanji>happenstance</kanji>.
故.on: Then a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala falls out of a tree and lands in the soup too.
故.kun: '<sound>You</sound> did this!' the old man tells the cat, who blinks and lays an <sound>e</sound>gg in reply.

現.meaning: A <part>king</part> points a <part>camera</part> at you and shouts: 'Smile!' Click. Not yesterday, not tomorrow: the photo shows you right here, right now, in the <kanji>present</kanji>.
現.on: 'A<sound>gain</sound>!' cries the king, and snaps you one more time, right now.
現.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>! <sound>Rah</sound>! <sound>Wah</sound>!' yells the crowd, as the king himself appears in the photo.

実.meaning: Under your <part>roof</part> stands the <part>Christmas tree</part> you thought you'd only dreamed of. You poke it, and real needles prick your finger. Real fruit hangs from its branches. It's no dream: it's <kanji>reality</kanji>.
実.on: '<sound>Gee</sound>!' you gasp, then sneeze at the pine smell: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
実.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat climbs the tree and picks you a piece of fruit.

房.meaning: A <part>door</part> has a little <part>sail</part> tied to its handle, and from the bottom of the sail hangs a fluffy bunch of threads that swings each time the door opens. Swish, swish: a <kanji>tassel</kanji>.
房.on: A <sound>bou</sound>lder rolls past the door, and the tassel waves at it.
房.kun: The cat swats the tassel instead of eating its <sound>foo</sound>d, a fat <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

作.meaning: A carpenter hangs his apron on a <part>coat hook</part>, then builds a whole <part>coat rack</part> out of spare planks, one peg at a time. Hammer, saw, glue. Give him some wood and he'll <kanji>make</kanji> something.
作.on: Then he plants a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent on top of the rack for decoration.
作.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes in the sawdust, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of a clock he made.

同.meaning: A photographer peers through a <part>frame</part> at a pair of twins. Draw <part>one</part> line across them: same eyebrows. Below it, a <part>mouth</part> each: same grin. You can't tell them apart: they're exactly the <kanji>same</kanji>.
同.on: They even bake bread from the very same lump of <sound>dough</sound>.
同.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' you laugh, as they both bite the same <sound>na</sound>an at once.
